languageVariant: Piedmontese literary spelling; introductory AI-authored examples awaiting native-speaker review
courseDescription: TEMPORARY UNREVIEWED AI-GENERATED SAMPLE. English to Piedmontese, with one Lesson per current named Exercise type. The content is for testing and requires native-speaker review before language-teaching use. Basic spellings were checked against Claudio Panero's English-Piedmontese dictionary; examples and letter diagrams are newly authored. Audio uses On-Device TTS with pms-IT. This demo contains no recorded Piedmontese voice. Listening examples require a suitable device voice; availability and pronunciation depend on the device.

lessons.title: Pick the translation (to target) — English to Piedmontese

content.text: Read the English source and pick its Piedmontese translation. ël can = the dog; ross = red; tre = three.
Pick the translation (to target): English to Piedmontese. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Pick the translation (to source) — Piedmontese to English

content.text: Read the Piedmontese source and pick its English meaning. bon-aneuit = good night; ël pan = the bread; mi i son content = I am happy.
Pick the translation (to source): Piedmontese to English. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Type the translation (to target) — Write in Piedmontese

content.text: Translate English into Piedmontese. Thank you accepts grassie or mersì. The happy speaker is masculine: i son content; mi is optional. The house is la ca.
Type the translation (to target): Write in Piedmontese. Three short examples use this exercise type.

content.text: grassie = thank you; la ca = the house; i son content = I am happy. Type the English meaning.

lessons.title: Build the translation (to target) — Translate with blocks

content.text: Build an English phrase in Piedmontese. ël lìber = the book; i son content = I am happy (masculine); pan e eva = bread and water. For I am happy, both mi i son content and i son content are accepted.
Build the translation (to target): Translate with blocks. Three short examples use this exercise type.

Build the translation (to source): Translate into English with blocks. Three short examples use this exercise type.

lessons.title: Match the words — Three translations

content.text: Match English words with Piedmontese words. Food: pan, eva, pom. Animals: gat, can, caval. At home: tàula, cadrega, pòrta.

prompt.text: Piedmontese has ël for masculine and la for feminine nouns; l' comes before a vowel: l'eva.
The subject pronoun is often doubled: mi i son means I am, literally me I am.
Bondì is good morning, bon-aneuit good night; ciàu works for hello and bye.
